title: AI arXiv daily — Friday, 13 November 2026 batch — 10 notable papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; the ordering is inferred from checkable discussion, conference/publication signals, citation totals, cross-list breadth, and artifacts. Citation evidence is limited for very recent papers, and current Semantic Scholar totals are not citations gained during this batch. For papers already published in proceedings or a journal, existing citations may predate the arXiv posting.

sections.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
sections.abstract: The authors introduce CRAM, a learned Hopfield–Tank energy for constraint puzzles, reporting near-perfect Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique accuracy after 42 ms and 132 ms of training, respectively, and at least 282× fewer inference FLOPs than looped baselines on the studied tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors train an explicit energy directly from solved puzzles and report data-efficient reasoning on Sudoku, maze, N-Queens, and graph-coloring tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors caution that the tested puzzles are unusually well matched to the pairwise energy; high scores do not establish scaling to harder tasks such as ARC-AGI, where learning latent quantities remains open.
sections.ranking_evidence: Several checkable signals appeared immediately: Ken Ashe published a technical discussion, World Neural posted a separate paper summary, and the authors released a public implementation. No current Semantic Scholar citations were reported at the snapshot; these are discussion and artifact signals, not readership statistics.

sections.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
sections.abstract: AgentSSL frames semi-supervised learning as agentic program search and reports that generated pipelines beat tuned human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings, while selection by the agent's feedback metric can reduce performance by as much as 47%.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors formulate semi-supervised learning as search over executable programs and introduce ProgramSelectBench to measure how well agents choose among candidate pipelines.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports that the supervised AgentSL variant matches AgentSSL on both ecology tasks; its search is biased toward SSL, and reliable program selection without labels remains unresolved.
sections.ranking_evidence: The arXiv record lists NeurIPS 2026, with a matching official NeurIPS poster and OpenReview record; the authors also provide a project site and a 16,977-program selection benchmark. These are checkable quality/artifact signals, not popularity counts.

sections.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
sections.abstract: NOPO formalizes settings where a verifier can reliably identify failures but cannot certify apparent successes, and updates a policy by suppressing trusted negatives rather than treating unverified positives as rewards.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine reference-relative suppression of verifier-negative samples with group-level weighting and report pass@k gains across code, logic, and math evaluations using unit-test, constraint, and LLM-based verifiers.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that negative-only learning specifies what to avoid but not where removed probability mass should move; using partial positive evidence without losing robustness remains future work.
sections.ranking_evidence: The arXiv record identifies acceptance at NeurIPS 2026 as a Spotlight, corroborated by the official NeurIPS poster page. No current Semantic Scholar citations were reported at the snapshot; the conference signal, rather than citation momentum, supports its placement.

sections.title: Collaborative Task Allocation for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems Through Iterative Clustering
sections.abstract: The paper introduces iterative clustering to split multi-robot task allocation into smaller assignments, proves monotonic utility improvement, and reports simulation gains over several heuristic baselines.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose random and heuristic iterative clustering variants, prove assignment utility rises monotonically, and report scalable simulations up to 1,000 robots and 500 tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evaluation is simulation-based; the authors identify decentralized implementations and dynamic or uncertain environments as future work.
sections.ranking_evidence: Semantic Scholar reports 10 citations and 1 influential citation as current totals; the arXiv record links the paper to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters and ICRA 2026, and the authors provide code. The journal/conference work predates this arXiv posting, so citation totals are not evidence of citations gained in this batch.

sections.title: Unibuc - NLP at "Voight-Kampff" Generative AI Detection PAN 2025
sections.abstract: The team compares LLM-embedding classifiers and fine-tuned models for PAN 2025 AI-text detection, reporting about 99.4% F1 for a classical-model ensemble on the sensitivity task and more modest results on human-AI collaborative text classification.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that majority voting over LightGBM, XGBoost, logistic regression, and SVM is comparable to fine-tuning for Subtask 1; their feature-fusion approach for Subtask 2 performs modestly.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper's error analysis highlights AI-generated fiction as difficult to distinguish; human-AI collaborative text classification also remains weak, with reported macro-F1 and recall around 0.43.
sections.ranking_evidence: Semantic Scholar reports 5 citations and 1 influential citation as current totals; a matching PAN at CLEF 2025 proceedings paper is independently available through CEUR-WS. This is an arXiv posting of earlier competition work, so these citations do not establish a new burst in the present batch.

sections.title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sections.abstract: By replacing facts in retrieved passages with counterfactual variants, the authors estimate that some cited claims come from parametric memory rather than retrieved context and find that standard natural-language-inference checks do not reliably detect this mismatch.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose counterfactual value substitution for separating retrieved facts from model-supplied parametric facts, compare ten attribution methods, and report that their best detector is not yet accurate enough to act on.
sections.unique_caveat: The tested model set covers five sizes from one family and one comparator family; the authors say the method measures what a model knew rather than what it actually used, leaving provenance separation open.
sections.ranking_evidence: Multiple recent third-party write-ups surfaced, including SyncAI News, Bharat Hunt, Agentic Design, and CASRAI. Semantic Scholar reports no current citations at the snapshot; these write-ups are attention signals, not validation of the method.

sections.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
sections.abstract: GeoWorld and LiveGeo create an evolving geographic environment and benchmark where agents must gather evidence, check whether it remains valid, and revise plans; the authors report that strong static performance does not ensure dynamic reliability.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors release GeoWorld with verifiable evolving state histories and LiveGeo tasks that test active information gathering, evidence revalidation, and replanning.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is specific to the proposed geographic tasks; the abstract does not establish reliability in other dynamic environments or real-world deployments.
sections.ranking_evidence: Recent summaries appeared from World Neural, AI Hot, and CASRAI. Semantic Scholar reports no current citations at the snapshot; the outside coverage is a modest attention signal, not evidence that the benchmark is widely adopted.

sections.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
sections.abstract: ISLA is a measure-weighted slice-attention transformer for steady boundary-driven PDEs that builds in rigid-motion and unit invariance and reports strong results on aerodynamic surrogate benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author claims coordinate-free learned operations, measure-weighted boundary aggregation, and read-only interior queries provide rigid-motion/reflection equivariance and mesh-consistent predictions under stated conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper states that unseen boundary layouts can sharply hurt accuracy, a deterministic equivariant predictor cannot represent symmetry-breaking flow modes, and 3D interior training can require more than 80 GiB per GPU.
sections.ranking_evidence: Semantic Scholar reports 1 citation, marked influential, as a current total; the paper is cross-listed across four categories and is explicitly paired with AeroZoo. An experimental NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo implementation page provides an additional checkable artifact signal.

sections.title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
sections.abstract: AeroZoo contributes 3,815 time-mean RANS flow problems across seven geometry families and eight enclosures, with 22 frozen evaluation splits intended to test generalization beyond single-family datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a benchmark with complete boundary-condition inputs and geometry-disjoint splits; their results report that boundary-condition tokens reduce GeoTransolver error on the random split.
sections.unique_caveat: The canonical benchmark uses only 2,816 cases with stable time means, and the authors report error increases of 2.4–9.2 times on some held-out enclosure or boundary-layout splits; the abstract says the data and scoring code will be released.
sections.ranking_evidence: Semantic Scholar reports 1 citation as a current total; the three-category cross-list and explicit companion link to ISLA make this a coherent benchmark/model pairing rather than an isolated architecture claim.

sections.title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
sections.abstract: Metal Sandbox combines per-agent filesystem isolation, native command execution, and cross-Mac scheduling, reporting higher command throughput on four Mac mini M4 nodes and reduced waiting in fixed-trace replays.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a native Apple Silicon execution environment that schedules agent tool commands across Macs and integrates with Harbor for task verification and rollout collection.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that this is not hostile multi-tenant containment or physical GPU exclusivity; replay estimates hold agent behavior and phase durations fixed, and the hardware evaluation uses four Macs.
sections.ranking_evidence: Semantic Scholar reports no current citations at the snapshot; the four-category cross-list, open-source Metal Sandbox and Harbor repositories, and concrete multi-node measurements support its relevance, but not a claim of popularity.
